section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
section_1.content: Briefly recap superposition and interference. Define diffraction as the bending of light around obstacles, analogous to water waves passing through a slit, which is the foundational mechanism for holography.
section_1.example: Visualize a ripple tank experiment where a plane wave hits a tiny aperture, creating a circular wave pattern.

section_2.title: The Mechanism of Holography: Recording Phase
section_2.content: Explain that standard photography captures only intensity (amplitude). Holography captures both amplitude and phase by using a reference beam to create an interference pattern on a medium.
section_2.example: Imagine two stones thrown into a pond simultaneously; the intersection of their ripples creates a unique, complex pattern of peaks and valleys—this is the interference pattern recorded on film.

section_3.title: The Reconstruction: Diffraction in Action
section_3.content: Describe how shining the reference beam back onto the recorded interference pattern (the hologram) acts like a diffraction grating. The light reconstructs the original wavefronts, creating a 3D image.
section_3.example: Visualize a laser beam hitting a 'frozen' ripples (the hologram), causing the light to bend precisely as it did when reflecting off the original object—the 'ghost' of an apple appears in space.

section_4.title: Mathematical Integration: The Fresnel-Kirchhoff Formula
section_4.content: Introduce the concept of wave propagation through an integral representation. Use an animation showing the light intensity distribution (I = |E_ref + E_obj|^2) mapping to the film.
section_4.example: A graphical overlay showing the math equation dynamically changing as the distance between the reference source and the object changes, visually demonstrating the complexity of the fringes.

section_5.title: Real-World Application: The Holographic Future
section_5.content: Conclude with modern applications of these principles, from high-density data storage to medical imaging and augmented reality displays.
section_5.example: A futuristic 'Iron Man' style HUD interface that uses holographic diffraction to project interactive 3D tactical maps into the pilot's field of view.

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map 6x6 to grid positions
                x = 2.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Fresnel-Kirchhoff describes wave propagation.", "We model light via an integral.", "Intensity patterns map to the film."]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Integration: The Fresnel-Kirchhoff Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define mobjects
        fk_formula = MathTex(r"U(P) = \frac{1}{i\lambda} \iint_S U \frac{e^{ikr}}{r} \cos \theta \, dS", color=WHITE)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        
        # Break down formula
        self.play(fk_formula.animate.set_opacity(0.3))
        # Place integral parts
        group = VGroup(*integral_elements).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(group, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(group))
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        
        # Highlight phase factor
        self.play(Indicate(group[2], color="#FFD700"))
        self.play(group[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):

        self.setup_layout("The Reconstruction: Diffraction in Action", lecture_lines)
